item.title: Amazon unveils new lineup of Alexa devices including redesigned Echo Show
item.description: Amazon.com on Wednesday unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices including a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart display and a photo frame with built-in Alexa, as it pushes its latest

item.title: US DOJ is inquiring about Nvidia's purchase of Hugging Face
item.description: The Justice Department's recent questioning covers Nvidia's acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether the chip designer has exerted pressure on its customers, the two people said.

item.title: Google misses Wall Street expectations, Alphabet stock sinks in early after-hours trading
item.description: The Mountain View, California-based company said its net income was $26.17 billion in the July-September period. That's down from $34.98 billion in the same period a year earlier.

item.title: Microsoft beats expectations fueled by Azure cloud business
item.description: Microsoft shares popped more than five percent Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, fueled by its Azure cloud computing division which grew by 48 percent in the September quarter. However, Google on Wednesday reported that revenue from its cloud division doubled to $30.7 billion during the quarter, bringing it closer to Microsoft's Azure revenue, which reached $33.2 billion in the same period.

item.title: DeepSeek, Moonshot used OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train latest models: report
item.description: Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's powerful GPT-6 Astra model to train their latest models, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Meesho Q2 loss narrows; Info Edge names Sanjeev Bikhchandani CEO
item.description: Happy Thursday! Meesho’s losses shrunk as revenue grew in the second quarter of FY27. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Anthropic tells California governor courts should be able to block risky AI models
item.description: Anthropic itself has faced government restrictions on its AI systems. The Trump administration in June ordered Anthropic to immediately restrict foreign access to its cyber-capable Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models, citing national security concerns. The US Commerce Department later lifted the order.

item.title: German startup NVision shows new path to quantum computing chips in Nature paper
item.description: Startups and tech giants such as Microsoft and IBM alike are racing to build quantum computers that hold the promise of solving problems that would take conventional machines thousands of years. But NVision, which has raised more than $155 million in funding from firms such as Abbott Laboratories, made the discovery published on Wednesday while working in an entirely different field: improving medical devices.

item.title: Meesho loss narrows; Sanjeev Bikhchandani back as Info Edge CEO
item.description: Meesho cut its losses in the July-September quarter, while growth continued. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Cognite reports $1 billion in verified AI value, confirming impact of industrial AI solutions
item.description: Driving approximately 36% of value verified to date, customers are leveraging AI and automated workflows to prevent costly asset shutdowns across complex industrial operations, help them get back running when the unexpected happens, and lower the costs of running their operations.

item.title: Meesho expects stronger Q3 growth due to change in festive sale timeline
item.description: The first day of Meesho's annual flagship sale, the Mega Blockbuster Sale, saw orders growing about 75% YoY. Its transacting customers increased by about 60% YoY.

item.title: Sherpa and the future of AI-powered storytelling at Pocket FM
item.description: Pocket FM is using AI to help writers bring their stories to life and reach listeners across the world. With Sherpa, its AI-powered writing partner, the company is making it easier to manage long storylines and develop characters while keeping the creative decisions in the hands of writers.

item.title: Delivery Hero raises full-year forecast again on strong Q3 growth
item.description: The company now expects gross merchandise value (GMV), a common metric for delivery firms measuring the total value of all goods sold through the market place, to grow 10%-12% this year, up from a previous forecast of 9%-11%.

item.title: China's new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels
item.description: The draft rules, released on October 16, distinguish between foreign customers using Chinese AI services and foreign companies obtaining the models, data or expertise needed to operate or reproduce them independently.

item.title: Agentic AI can cut banks' transaction monitoring workload by up to 50%: McKinsey
item.description: Banks could reduce the human effort required for transaction monitoring investigations by 30-50% by deploying agentic artificial intelligence (AI), while improving the quality and consistency of compliance reports, according to a report by McKinsey.

item.title: AI chips worth $12.1 million seized at Malaysia airport, customs authority says
item.description: Malaysian customs said on Wednesday that it had seized about 49.5 million ringgit ($12.11 million) worth of advanced artificial intelligence chips this month, as

item.title: China's CXMT to start advanced AI memory production despite poor yields
item.description: The decision highlights China's intense shortage of the AI memory chips, which are essential to a government-backed push to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI processors at scale amid US curbs on access to foreign-made technology.

item.title: TPG pursues $5 billion acquisition of British data centre group Ark: FT
item.description: Global alternative asset manager TPG is in talks to buy British data centre group Ark from Elliott Investment Management at a valuation of about $5 billion, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Indian IT firms poised to benefit from enterprise AI adoption as infrastructure costs rise: Report
item.description: Indian information technology (IT) companies are well-positioned to benefit from the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) by enterprises, as rising infrastructure investments and funding requirements increase financial risks for companies building and operating AI computing capacity, according to a research report by Anand Rathi.

item.title: AI chip giant SK hynix says quarterly operating profit soars 630%
item.description: South Korean chip giant SK hynix said Wednesday its third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent on-year, largely driven by the artificial intelligence industry's explosive demand for its advanced memory chips. The memory chip giant said it had posted record revenue and operating profit for six straight quarters since the second quarter of last year.

item.title: Oracle's Larry Ellison dismisses 'SaaS apocalypse' fears, says AI will make software better
item.description: Speaking at Oracle AI World here, Ellison, the company's executive chairman and chief technology officer, rejected talk of a "SaaS apocalypse", in which businesses would use AI to build their own applications instead of buying software-as-a-service (SaaS) products.

item.title: India among Oracle NetSuite's highest-priority markets, says Asia head Amit Suxena
item.description: Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of Oracle AI World, Amit Suxena, group vice president and head of Asia at Oracle NetSuite, an AI-native business management platform, said momentum among Indian businesses had been growing over the last four to five years.

item.title: US agency approves Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion acquisition of Globalstar
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission said Tuesday it has approved Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion deal to acquire Globalstar as the retail giant's satellite arm aims to build a satellite-based communications network to take on Elon Musk's SpaceX Starlink unit.

item.title: Nearly 60% of firms yet to move AI beyond pilots as deployment remains key challenge: Report
item.description: Nearly 60 per cent of organisations surveyed remain in the exploration or pilot stages of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, with only around 40 per cent having moved to production or scaling, highlighting the challenge businesses face in deploying AI across their operations, according to a report by Citi Institute.

item.title: Meta, Snap head to trial in another case about social media's harms
item.description: Jury selection is expected to begin on Wednesday in Los Angeles for another landmark trial about the alleged harms of social media on young users, with Meta and, for the first time, Snap as defendants. Meta and YouTube lost the first so-called bellwether case earlier this year, when a jury found them collectively liable for harming a young user known by the initials KGM, and ordered the tech companies to pay a combined $6 million penalty.

item.title: Anthropic's record IPO faces some big questions
item.description: No startup has ever grown so fast. Investors have already grown nervous.

item.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips
item.description: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing a person familiar with the matter, as technology companies ramp up spending on data centers and semiconductors to meet surging demand for AI computing.

item.title: US agency is again probing if Polymarket broke 2022 settlement, sources says
item.description: A US regulator is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban US users from its main overseas platform, reviving an inquiry the agency shuttered last year without bringing

item.title: Cognizant eyes Sarvam stake; Ather aims for higher market share
item.description: Happy Wednesday! Cognizant has held discussions to invest in homegrown AI startup Sarvam. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Snabbit's Aayush Agarwal on the $100B Home Services Opportunity | The Brand Equity Show
Swiss AI drug trial startup receives funding from Spotify-backer Creandum
item.description: An AI foundation model, trained on about two million human RNA readouts, would replace these and animal testing with 12-week simulations, the company said.

item.title: Anthropic IPO rocks Indian IT; Why Walmart is in no hurry to list Flipkart
item.description: Anthropic’s US IPO filing sent Indian IT stocks lower on Tuesday. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Big Tech earnings a test of the AI boom amid market turmoil
item.description: Investors are pressing for evidence that the AI boom can deliver swift returns to justify its enormous price tag. Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave and record costs to insure Meta Platform's debt have amplified concerns about how the massive AI infrastructure buildout is being funded, particularly as higher US interest rates loom.

item.title: In China, the AI bubble has already burst
item.description: While global tech stocks teeter, in China they have already crashed as lofty valuations collapse under worries about AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports.

item.title: Paytm has proven the resilience of its merchant-led model: JP Morgan
item.description: In its latest report titled "First Take: All-round beat", JP Morgan said Paytm's focus on its merchant franchise and sharp cost control following the resolution of regulatory restrictions has helped the company achieve EBIT breakeven, proving the resilience of its merchant-led model.

item.title: Tata Motors, Amazon partner to deploy 3,000 electric trucks for ecommerce logistics
item.description: Heavy Industries Minister H D Kumaraswamy flagged off the initial fleet of trucks. "I congratulate Tata Motors and Amazon on this significant collaboration to deploy 3,000 electric trucks across Amazon's transportation network in India," Kumaraswamy said.

item.title: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming reclaims top spot in China's rich list, thanks to his firm's AI push
item.description: The rankings released by The Hurun Research Institute on Tuesday reflected that the country's high-tech sectors were rising but others like consumer and real estate were under pressure.

item.title: Alibaba AI model secretly tried to reach Beijing server in test, rival Cohere says
item.description: Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday one of Alibaba's Qwen AI models tried to send data to an Alibaba Cloud storage server in Beijing during a security test. The model made the attempt even though its own reasoning indicated it would not do such a thing, Cohere said.

item.title: Australia warns of 'unprecedented' AI threat
item.description: Artificial intelligence poses an "unprecedented" threat as foreign governments turn it loose to hack computer networks and critical infrastructure, Australia's cyber security agency warned on Tuesday. "This activity extends beyond government networks, and includes critical infrastructure entities, private businesses and individuals."

item.title: Risks spelled out for Anthropic investors include possible harms from runaway AI
item.description: The risks laid out by the San Francisco company in its filing Monday with the Securities and Exchange Commission included discussion of bad actors potentially using AI models to build deadly weapons or the technology itself going rogue with untold consequences.

item.title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos
item.description: On Monday, Instagram announced that it is testing out video lengths of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the US.

item.title: DoorDash in talks to buy Instacart in roughly $17 billion deal
item.description: DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery-delivery platform at about $17 billion, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday.

item.title: Anthropic IPO by the numbers, from a possible valuation in the trillions to surging revenue
item.description: The artificial intelligence lab filed papers Monday setting up a Wall Street debut next month, ahead of its chief rival OpenAI and just months after SpaceX set records in June with an initial public offering that raised $86 billion.

item.title: Why Walmart would rather keep Flipkart private, for now
item.description: Over the past few weeks, much has been written about former employees of the online commerce company writing to Walmart's board, asking for liquidity on the stock options they were granted 10 to 15 years ago. On October 1, at least eight former senior executives, among them former Myntra CEO Mukesh Bansal and former chief business officer Ankit Nagori, wrote to Walmart chairman Gregory Penner, other board members and Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy, seeking a complete exit for all former employees holding vested options.

item.title: VerSe valuation sinks; Paytm Q2 profit rises
item.description: Happy Tuesday! Dailyhunt parent VerSe Innovation’s valuation has taken a sharp hit. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Apple iPhone Duo cracked screen: Tech giant says it will replace folding smartphones with display problems days after mega launch
item.description: Apple did not comment on what might cause the iPhone Duo cracked screen issue. Apple acknowledged the problems on Monday, saying affected units tend to show the problem quickly.

item.title: Ather rides to profit; Pronto's US AI play
item.description: Ather Energy swung to profit in the July-September quarter. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

item.title: Anthropic is said to plan public filing for Mega-IPO Monday
item.description: Anthropic PBC plans to file for an initial public offering in New York on Monday morning. The artificial intelligence model maker is expected to begin its marketing efforts by November 9. The anticipated IPO aims to rival the size of SpaceX's previous offering, according to industry sources.

item.title: How to compare real trading costs across forex trading apps in India
item.description: When choosing a forex trading platform, it's important to analyze charges, commissions, and transactional fees. Comparing the overall cost of trade execution is advisable, specifically during peak trading times. For those who trade on the move, testing mobile trading apps for performance and connectivity is vital. Funding and withdrawal charges also affect total expenses, particularly for traders with smaller accounts.

item.title: US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters
item.description: US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies.
